words.gloss: a split fraction of a sesame seed
is indeed of very small measure

literal: Like a split fraction of a sesame seed, even though it is of such small measure, if internal enmity exists, ruin will happen.
translation: Even if it is as minuscule as a split sesame seed, if internal enmity exists within, ruin is certain to follow.
modern: எள்ளின் பிளவைப் போன்ற மிகச் சிறிய அளவு உடையதாக இருந்தாலும், ஒருவரிடம் உட்பகை இருக்குமானால் அழிவு நிச்சயம் உண்டாகும்.
explanation: This couplet warns of the devastating power of internal discord. The poet uses the metaphor of a split sesame seed ('எட்பகவு') to represent the smallest possible unit of division. Even if the internal enmity is as tiny and seemingly insignificant as this fraction, its mere presence ('உள்ளது') guarantees complete ruin ('கேடு'). The lesson is that internal division, no matter how small, must never be tolerated as it inevitably leads to destruction.
